title: Arranger task extraction + dataset rights proof on real admitted PDMX (Wave Q, Q-05 — Tier B + training gate 2)
whatWasRun: extract-arranger-tasks.mjs over 5,000 randomly sampled PDMX MIDI files that pass BOTH the licence gate and the authors' no_license_conflict.txt, with a work-level train/val/test split (90/5/5 by a hash of the work id).
taskDefinition: given the structure plus every track except one, over an 8-bar window, predict the held-out track. The target is a real human-written part; the model learns from human choices, not a teacher's imitation.

datasetRightsProof.meaning: Every one of 3,577 training examples traces to a work admitted by both our licence gate and the authors' own subset. assertTrainingMayProceed() passes. A run whose proof does not verify does not start.

theFindingThatMatters.what: Only 9% of sampled PDMX scores yield an arranger task. The other 91% are single-track or under 8 bars.
theFindingThatMatters.why: PDMX is overwhelmingly solo piano and solo-instrument sheet music, not multitrack arrangements. A score with one track has no 'rest of the arrangement' to condition on.
theFindingThatMatters.implication: PDMX at 222,856 works gives roughly 20,000 multitrack scores and — at ~8 tasks each after the cap — on the order of 150,000-200,000 arranger training examples. That is a real corpus but not a large one for a 200-350M model trained from scratch, and it is heavily weighted toward keys and drums as targets, with bass and guitar under-represented.
theFindingThatMatters.consequenceForThePlan: This is direct evidence for the from-scratch-vs-foundation question the model-discovery mission exists to answer. It strengthens the case for starting from an existing multitrack foundation and fine-tuning on PDMX, rather than training ARRANGER_FM from scratch on PDMX alone. The tournament decides.

honestLimits: 5,000-score sample, not the full 222,856. The yield rate and family distribution are estimates; a full pass would firm them up.

No near-duplicate detection yet. PDMX has known duplicate arrangements of popular pieces; the work-level split protects against leakage between splits but not against the same piece appearing many times within train.
The task is 8-bar windowed part-prediction. Whole-song form, long-range development and cross-section coherence are not in this task formulation — they need a hierarchical or long-context variant.
No model has consumed a single one of these tasks. This is the corpus and the rights proof, not a trained model.
